rulings.item: (1) Is I-60 a system-wide mandatory authority?
rulings.recommendation: NO. It is mandatory only for the new-rack paths it enumerates.
rulings.reasoning: The Owner rule is worded broadly ('every NEW logical rack', decisions I-60.md:11). The frozen scope, however, is closed by where a creation comes from: Freeze §4 has a table of six paths plus the A-1 menu batch cases, and explicitly says 'Nunca ... proyeccion, duplicacion, layout'. §5 puts RACKDUPLICAR and RACKLAYOUT out of scope by analogy as copies, with Owner authorization, even though they also mint new RackIds. The code (RackNewRackName.cs:9-12) and the guard N-6 enforce exclusion only; nothing forces every creation path to call the allocator. No ADR makes I-60 a system-wide invariant.

rulings.item: (2) Does RACKMIRROR have a legitimate exception, or is it out of I-60's scope?
rulings.recommendation: It is out of I-60's scope by copy provenance. No I-52 exception is needed.
rulings.reasoning: A mirror does create a new logical rack in identity terms: NewRackId per group, and PDC-1 'nunca conserva el RackId en la copia'. But it is a copy-provenance operation: PDC-1 'Solo copia'; V17 §9 reuses the I-51 duplication assigner with an injected name policy, RACKDUPLICAR the historical one and RACKMIRROR '<base> - espejo'; §10.1 reaches the name through Compose + RackEnvelopeRestamp; and the path is caller-owned creation (SL-1/SL-2/SL-4), never DrawSelectiveView. It is the same class of operation I-60 §5 excludes, RACKDUPLICAR. The only gap is that RACKMIRROR is not named in I-60 (it does not exist in main), which is a disclosure item (NR-01), not an exception.

rulings.item: (3) Would adopting I-60 change Proposal or contract semantics?
rulings.recommendation: YES for Proposal V17. NO for the CT-21D contract text.
rulings.reasoning: Adoption would replace PDC-2, ID-4, §10.1 step 5, T-M05, T-M26, P9, M-1 and M-8, and remove source traceability. Since '<base> - espejo' is never unassigned, adoption would also require a new rule (for example 'always allocate', or 'allocate only for a blank base'), which is an I-52 amendment and outside I-60's frozen scope. It would add a lock and read transaction before T_M (RackNewRackName.cs:35-43), which reopens BA-06 PREPARE-R and BA-08 §15. CT-21D V2.x §15.5 fixes only block names and NewRackId, so its text is unaffected. The SL-Y 'added' trigger is invariant, because both policies give non-blank names.

rulings.item: (4) Does the mirror suffix still have semantic or user-facing value?
rulings.recommendation: YES.
rulings.reasoning: The suffix is the only persisted link from a mirror to its source (the RackId is new, and the ID-2 old-to-new map is not persisted). It separates source and mirror in RACKLISTA, the BOM and the drawn name label (T-M26, M-1). It gives recognisable block names ('<base> - espejo - planta'). With a blank legacy base it yields 'Rack - espejo', never blank, which already meets I-60's goal of a non-blank, readable, editable name. It never matches I-60's exact '<Prefijo> N' pattern, so it cannot disturb I-60 numbering. The user can still edit it (I-60 goal: 'editable').

rulings.item: (5) Is a new naming contract required?
rulings.recommendation: NO.
rulings.reasoning: PDC-2 (V17, inherited by V18 §7) and the I-60 Freeze §4/§5 exclusion together already determine the mirror name without conflict. A disclosure row in the I-52 decisions (NR-01) and a future implementation guard (NR-02) are enough. A new contract would be needed only if the Owner later decides to bring RACKMIRROR under I-60.

That path is I60_MUST_GOVERN_REQUIRES_I52_AMENDMENT: amend V17 PDC-2/ID-4/§10.1/T-M05/T-M26/M-1/M-8, add a new BA-06 PREPARE-R row and reopen BA-08 §15, and make an explicit Owner product decision extending I-60 beyond its frozen new-rack table. The reconciliation (Decision A) does not authorize that.

reviews.verdict: NAMING_COMPATIBLE_NO_CHANGE. The historical requirement stands: V17 PDC-2 gives the mirror the name "<base> - espejo", with no ordinal, never blank, and 'Rack - espejo' for a blank base. It is inherited by Freeze V18 §7 and is I-52's own authority. I-60 is not mandatory system-wide. By its own Freeze §4/§5 it applies only to new-rack paths and excludes copy-provenance operations (duplication, layout, projection). RACKMIRROR is a copy-provenance creation (PDC-1, the V17 §9 reuse of the I-51 assigner, caller-owned seams) and never passes through the I-60 entry points. The two policies cannot conflict at runtime: the mirror name is never 'unassigned' and never matches the '<Prefijo> N' pattern. The CT-21D contract V2.1..V2.5 does not fix the logical name and needs no change. Every baseline fact that depends on the mirror name is UNCHANGED at 95690c28: the writer constants, ORACLE_SPEC, BA-08 §15, and the mirror half of SL-Y 'added'. The FX-ANN-BLANK source half is ARTIFACT_UPDATE_REQUIRED under the already-issued AR5-11; that is an I-60 effect on source racks, not on mirror naming. Required actions, all minor: record the NR-01 disclosure row, add the NR-02 guard at implementation, and fix the NR-03 citations. No Owner choice is needed. Adopting I-60 for RACKMIRROR would need a separate explicit Owner decision and an I-52 amendment (I60_MUST_GOVERN_REQUIRES_I52_AMENDMENT). Reconciliation Decision A does not authorize that.

Its facts are no longer discarded: they feed RackSingleViewRequirementReporting.ForHeaderPlan, which contradicts the U-09 row ("Facts are discarded"). AR5-03 moves U-09 to OC-PREP-READ. It appends a rotated reference with no jig, and it imports through its own Observe call (RackProjectionCommandPort.cs:110). By the logic of V2.4 §1's last sentence, an added operation reopens the review of its class. So "confirm-only with the product rows added" is not admissible. AR5-13 places the re-verification inside that round ("La ronda de re-ligado los re-verifica en el SHA ligado"). AR5-14 also requires the BA-11 row for BA-01 to carry the prerequisites of the SHA decision and of AR5-13. Today the bound SHA is only a Coordinator proposal, and the round has not been opened. A read-only assessment cannot stand in for the bound-SHA decision, or for the Architect's review of the re-verification, before the effective contract is recorded as AGREED.

(2) Substance. The finding that "no clause is contradicted" is not safe. V2.1 15.1 F-1, which AR5-13 names explicitly, says Selective frontal and planta definitions are created by SystemBlockWriter.CreateBlock, which calls the library importer. It also says "Each view is a separate call and a separate transaction; sibling views are grouped by the envelope id, not by an atomic unit". At 95690c28 this no longer holds for all Selective paths:

That creates the definition with the new SystemBlockWriter.CreatePreparedBlock, which has no importer call; the import runs separately in HeaderRequirements.
- With deferred sibling redraws, BlockPlacement.PlaceDefinitionWithoutCleanup(..., beforeCommit) applies SiblingRedrawTransaction.ApplyInTransaction inside the same jig transaction that appends the new reference. The code comment reads "Mode-2 placement: prepared sibling writes share the first jig transaction after OK".

This is the Architect's own IMP-05 (two of the three Selective entries no longer reach the inventoried chain). So a 15.1 row is contradicted at the proposed bound SHA. AR3-12 is already recorded as superseded (IMP-03). Whether a dated fact that is now contradicted counts as a "contradicted clause" (V2.6 needed) or stays a harmless dated fact is an Architect ruling under AR5-13. The re-verification cannot settle it by itself. Until that ruling exists, the conservative outcome is: CONTRACT EFECTIVO CT-21D-V2.5 = NOT_YET_AGREED. Record it AGREED only after (a) the Coordinator formally binds the SHA after the reconciliation CI, and (b) the Architect rules on the F-1 delta (and on the other 15.1, 15.8 and §25 rows) as V2.6-not-required.

The side statements are correct but do not save the ruling: agreement would not make BA-01 a candidate (the rule-5 agreement on BA-11 is still needed), it authorizes no host work or src changes, and NOT_YET_ADOPTED leaves §15.5 and PDC-2 as written.
